I implemented `AddMember` in `members.go`, but I could not run it: the permission settings blocked `go test` and `go vet`, so the code is not compiled or tested.

To handle the app's repeated requests, it skips the add if the name is already in the file, so a second identical request changes nothing. The catch is that two different people with the same name can't both be members. If that must be allowed, the app has to send a unique ID with each request, and the function has to check that ID instead of the name.

It also locks so two requests can't write at the same time. It writes to a temp file and renames it over the real file, so a crash can't leave the file half-written. The lock only covers one server process, not several.

**TLDR**
`AddMember` ignores a name that is already in the file, so a repeated request is safe. Not compiled or tested, because `go test` was blocked.
Decide: whether two members can share a name. If yes, requests need a unique ID.
